title: On the Power of Source Screening for Learning Shared Feature Extractors
abstract: arXiv:2602.16125v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Learning with shared representation is widely recognized as an effective way to separate commonalities from heterogeneity across various heterogeneous sources. Most existing work includes all related data sources via simultaneously training a common feature extractor and source-specific heads. It is well understood that data sources with low relevance or poor quality may hinder representation learning. In this paper, we further dive into the question of which data sources should be learned jointly by focusing on the traditionally deemed ``good'' collection of sources, in which individual sources have similar relevance and qualities with respect to the true underlying common structure. Towards tractability, we focus on the linear setting where sources share a low-dimensional subspace. We find that source screening can play a central role in statistically optimal subspace estimation. We show that, for a broad class of problem instances

translated_title: 关于源筛选在学习共享特征提取器中的威力研究
translated_abstract: 共享表示学习被广泛认为是分离各种异构源中共性与异质性的有效方法。现有大多数工作通过同时训练一个公共特征提取器和各源特定的头部来包含所有相关数据源。众所周知，低相关性或质量差的数据源可能会阻碍表示学习。在本文中，我们进一步深入探讨哪些数据源应该被联合学习的问题，重点关注传统上被视为“优质”的源集合，其中各个源相对于真实潜在公共结构具有相似的相关性和质量。为了便于处理，我们聚焦于线性设置，其中各源共享一个低维子空间。我们发现，源筛选在统计最优的子空间估计中可以发挥核心作用。我们证明，对于一大类问题实例，源筛选能显著提升估计性能。
tldr: 本文证明在共享表示学习中，即使面对质量相似的源，进行源筛选也能在统计上显著提升子空间估计的最优性，这是传统方法忽略的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that source screening, even among sources of similar quality, plays a central role in achieving statistically optimal subspace estimation in shared representation learning, a factor overlooked by traditional methods.
